defect.locator_note: ^rule-inventory; Opperman/Wells support the vehicle-policy/anti-pretext rule, while Lafayette/Bertine are needed for the added booking and discretion breadth.
defect.problem: The black-letter rule is broadly supportable from the disclosed lake records, but the callout cites only Opperman and Wells. Those vehicle-inventory citations do not themselves carry the booking-inventory branch or the officer-discretion/suspicion formulation; disclosed support for those pieces comes from Lafayette and Bertine.
defect.proposed_fix: Add Illinois v. Lafayette, 462 U.S. 640, 648 (1983), after the booking clause, and Colorado v. Bertine, 479 U.S. 367, 375 (1987), for cabined discretion and non-suspicion basis; or narrow the callout to vehicle inventories only.

reasons: Opperman pin-376/pin-376a support routine inventories of lawfully impounded vehicles under standard police procedures being not unreasonable.
Wells pin-4/pin-4a support standardized criteria, anti-pretext, and an inventory-purpose policy.

Lafayette pin-648 is the disclosed support for booking inventories without warrant or probable cause; Bertine pin-375 is the disclosed support for discretion exercised under standard criteria and not suspicion of evidence, but neither is cited in the callout.
